use: The casual word; muryou is what signs and staff say.

example.romaji: kono ibento, tada de haireru n datte.
example.ja: このイベント、タダで入れるんだって。
example.english: Apparently you can get into this event for free.

examplePolite.romaji: kono ibento wa tada de haireru sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: このイベントはタダで入れるそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear you can get into this event for free.

notes: The same sound also means just or only: tada no tomodachi (just a friend).

example.romaji: koko, genkin shika tsukaenai yo.
example.ja: ここ、現金しか使えないよ。
example.english: This place only takes cash.

examplePolite.romaji: koko wa genkin shika tsukaemasen.
examplePolite.ja: ここは現金しか使えません。
examplePolite.english: This place only takes cash.

notes: Genkin na hito is someone who only helps when there's something in it for them.

use: Common on bills and with shop staff; with friends you'd more often use the verb harau.

example.romaji: shiharai wa kaado de ii?
example.ja: 支払いはカードでいい？
example.english: Okay if I pay by card?

examplePolite.romaji: shiharai wa kaado de ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 支払いはカードでいいですか？
examplePolite.english: Can I pay by card?

notes: Staff say oshiharai, as in oshiharai houhou wa? (how will you pay?).

use: The standard word on signs, menus and from staff; tada is the casual one.

example.romaji: koko no waifai, muryou da yo.
example.ja: ここのWi-Fi、無料だよ。
example.english: The Wi-Fi here is free.

examplePolite.romaji: koko no waifai wa muryou desu.
examplePolite.ja: ここのWi-Fiは無料です。
examplePolite.english: The Wi-Fi here is free.

notes: The opposite is yuuryou (paid). Free refills read okawari muryou.

example.romaji: a, otsuri moratte nai kamo.
example.ja: あ、おつりもらってないかも。
example.english: Oh, I don't think I got my change.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, otsuri o moratte inai n desu ga.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、おつりをもらっていないんですが。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, I didn't get my change.

notes: Staff hand it over saying otsuri desu. There's no tipping, so you always take it.

use: Where you pay in any shop; reji bukuro is a shopping bag.

example.romaji: reji sugoi naranderu ne.
example.ja: レジすごい並んでるね。
example.english: There's a huge line at the checkout.

examplePolite.romaji: reji ga sugoku konde imasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: レジがすごく混んでいますね。
examplePolite.english: The checkout is really busy.

use: The till slip; a formal receipt for expenses is a ryoushuusho.

example.romaji: reshiito mada aru? henpin shitai n da.
example.ja: レシートまだある？返品したいんだ。
example.english: Do you still have the receipt? I want to return it.

examplePolite.romaji: reshiito wa mada arimasu ka? henpin shitai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: レシートはまだありますか？返品したいんです。
examplePolite.english: Do you still have the receipt? I'd like to return it.

notes: To decline one at the till, say reshiito wa ii desu.

use: The default among friends; warikan ni suru = split it.

example.romaji: kyou wa warikan ni shiyou.
example.ja: 今日は割り勘にしよう。
example.english: Let's split the bill today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa warikan ni shimashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は割り勘にしましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we split the bill today?

notes: The opposite is ogoru (to treat someone).

use: A shop's bargain period; never 'sale' as in selling something.

example.romaji: ima seeru chuu da kara, yasui yo.
example.ja: 今セール中だから、安いよ。
example.english: There's a sale on now, so it's cheap.

examplePolite.romaji: ima seeru chuu na node, yasui desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 今セール中なので、安いですよ。
examplePolite.english: There's a sale on now, so it's cheap.

use: Short for tsuushin hanbai; now it mostly means buying online.

example.romaji: kore, tsuuhan de katta n da.
example.ja: これ、通販で買ったんだ。
example.english: I bought this online.

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa tsuuhan de katta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: これは通販で買ったんです。
examplePolite.english: I bought this online.

notes: Netto de katta (bought it online) means the same.

use: A set amount or percent off; gakusei waribiki = student discount.

example.romaji: gakuseishou misetara waribiki ni naru yo.
example.ja: 学生証見せたら割引になるよ。
example.english: You get a discount if you show your student ID.

examplePolite.romaji: gakuseishou o miseru to waribiki ni narimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 学生証を見せると割引になります。
examplePolite.english: You get a discount if you show your student ID.

notes: Percent off is counted in tenths: sanwaribiki = 30% off. A store-wide sale is a seeru.

use: Shizen ni also means naturally, without forcing it.

example.romaji: inaka wa shizen ga ookute ii ne.
example.ja: 田舎は自然が多くていいね。
example.english: The countryside's nice, there's so much nature.

examplePolite.romaji: inaka wa shizen ga ookute ii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 田舎は自然が多くていいですね。
examplePolite.english: The countryside is nice, with so much nature.

notes: Shizen na = natural, as in shizen na kanji (a natural feel).

example.romaji: mite, sora ga sugoi kirei.
example.ja: 見て、空がすごいきれい。
example.english: Look, the sky's so pretty.

examplePolite.romaji: mite kudasai, sora ga sugoku kirei desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 見てください、空がすごくきれいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Look, the sky is really beautiful.

example.romaji: koko, hoshi ga yoku mieru ne.
example.ja: ここ、星がよく見えるね。
example.english: You can really see the stars here.

examplePolite.romaji: koko wa hoshi ga yoku miemasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: ここは星がよく見えますね。
examplePolite.english: You can really see the stars here.

notes: Also star ratings: hoshi mittsu = three stars.

example.romaji: kawa no hou made sanpo shiyou ka.
example.ja: 川のほうまで散歩しようか。
example.english: Shall we walk down to the river?

examplePolite.romaji: kawa no hou made sanpo shimashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: 川のほうまで散歩しましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we take a walk down to the river?

notes: Kawa also means skin or leather; context tells them apart.

use: The view in front of you, usually a nice one.

example.romaji: koko kara no keshiki, saikou da ne.
example.ja: ここからの景色、最高だね。
example.english: The view from here is amazing.

examplePolite.romaji: koko kara no keshiki wa saikou desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: ここからの景色は最高ですね。
examplePolite.english: The view from here is wonderful.

example.romaji: doubutsu suki? uchi, inu katteru yo.
example.ja: 動物好き？うち、犬飼ってるよ。
example.english: Do you like animals? We've got a dog.

examplePolite.romaji: doubutsu wa suki desu ka? uchi wa inu o katte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 動物は好きですか？うちは犬を飼っています。
examplePolite.english: Do you like animals? We have a dog.

use: The spring blossom everyone goes out to see; ohanami is the picnic under it.

example.romaji: sakura, mou saiteru ne.
example.ja: 桜、もう咲いてるね。
example.english: The cherry blossoms are already out.

examplePolite.romaji: sakura ga mou saite imasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 桜がもう咲いていますね。
examplePolite.english: The cherry blossoms are already out.

notes: Sakura ga saku = they bloom; chiru = they fall.

example.romaji: ima no jishin, kekkou yureta ne.
example.ja: 今の地震、結構揺れたね。
example.english: That earthquake just now really shook.

examplePolite.romaji: ima no jishin, kekkou yuremashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今の地震、結構揺れましたね。
examplePolite.english: That earthquake just now really shook.

notes: Goes with yureru (shake). Jishin also means self-confidence; context tells them apart.

use: Older people use it for any phone message; for chat apps younger people say rain (LINE).

example.romaji: ato de meeru suru ne.
example.ja: 後でメールするね。
example.english: I'll email you later.

examplePolite.romaji: ato de meeru shimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 後でメールしますね。
examplePolite.english: I'll email you later.

notes: Meeru suru = send one; meeru ga kita = I got one.
